items.title: Reconcile the trusted RED-to-GREEN enforcement execution plan
items.context: Update the existing v7 program plan against current 0.3.294 code and the trusted RED-evidence decision spec. Define RED, GREEN, v1, v2, docsExempt, characterizationRequired, and redRequired; current-vs-target truth; mechanical tri-class classification; trusted RED and exact-target GREEN contracts; lifecycle doors; legacy adoption; concurrency; adversarial evidence; rollout order; acceptance tests; and explicit non-goals. The document remains a program plan and must not claim runtime enforcement already exists.
items.userSees: The plan opens with a status header stating that it supersedes v7, that 0.3.294 does not yet enforce the target policy, and which prerequisite workstream comes next; it then provides a definitions table and ordered workstream sections covering classification, trusted RED, same-target GREEN, migration, gate wiring, concurrency, rollout, and acceptance.
excludes: Creating RED or GREEN runtime evidence commands
Treating the plan as implemented authority

happy.desc: The plan defines a complete ordered program from trusted RED production through same-target GREEN consumption and enforcement rollout.
Every statement about current behavior is linked to a current code or configuration source and is distinct from target behavior.

edge.desc: Pure refactors use pre-change characterization and post-change equivalence rather than a synthetic failing RED.
Only mechanically proven non-executable documentation, research, and audit scope can use docsExempt, while retaining the complete lifecycle.

adversarial.desc: The plan prevents author-declared paths, Story type, labels, or prose from granting docsExempt.
The plan prevents RED captured after implementation or against a non-ancestor baseline from satisfying the gate.
The plan prevents caller-authored legacy v1 fields from satisfying post-adoption trusted RED requirements.
The plan covers rollback, compatibility, direct-terminal, and pre-write transition doors without equivalent-credential bypass.
The plan defines serialization and fork rejection for concurrent evidence writers and transitions.
The plan rejects stale, mismatched, quarantined, incomplete, or unsupported evidence chains.

items.title: Freeze and independently audit the candidate plan with Claude CLI
items.context: After CHK-001 and CHK-003 agree on the stable named section, freeze candidate plan bytes and launch a fresh read-only Claude CLI session that receives only those bytes and the audit rubric, with no authoring conversation and no repository edit permission. Record tool version, timestamp, plan SHA-256, exact rubric, raw response SHA-256, findings, truth-source adjudication, accepted changes, rejected suggestions, and final verdict in the audit Markdown file. CHK-002 owns any audit-driven plan revision; a section-name change reopens CHK-003 before the next freeze. Run at most three frozen-candidate rounds. APPROVE permits lifecycle review and no plan bytes may change afterward; any later revision voids the digest and blocks acceptance unless a remaining round audits it. A third non-APPROVE records the blocker, leaves this Story incomplete, and names a follow-up design revision.
items.userSees: A reproducible Claude CLI audit record whose final plan SHA-256 is recomputed immediately before lifecycle review; it ends with either APPROVE and the next implementation workstream, or a named blocking finding and the need for a follow-up design revision.
excludes: Allowing Claude CLI to modify repository files
Treating an APPROVE response as implementation evidence
Auditing mutable or unhashed plan bytes

happy.desc: The final audit records Claude CLI version, exact final-plan SHA-256, exact rubric, response SHA-256, and an APPROVE verdict for those bytes.

edge.desc: No more than three frozen-candidate audit rounds are run; unavailable, timed-out, or non-APPROVE outcomes remain explicitly blocked.
The recorded final-plan SHA-256 is recomputed after all audit-driven revisions and matches the bytes accepted by the final Claude response.

adversarial.desc: The audit record distinguishes external reviewer opinion from signed Proof-or-Stop lifecycle evidence and current runtime truth.

items.title: Replace the trusted RED-evidence specification's fragile plan line reference
items.context: After CHK-001 establishes the stable Workstream 2 section name and before CHK-002 freezes a candidate, replace the trusted RED-evidence subsystem specification's mutable line-number citation with that named section. If an audit-driven revision changes the section name, reopen this item and repair the backlink before freezing the next candidate. Do not change the subsystem's normative semantics.
items.userSees: The trusted RED-evidence specification links to the named program workstream and remains correct when the execution plan gains or loses lines.
excludes: Rewriting the trusted RED-evidence subsystem specification

happy.desc: The specification references the revised plan by document path and stable section name rather than mutable line numbers.

edge.desc: The backlink repair does not change the specification's normative RED-evidence semantics.

adversarial.desc: No stale Workstream 2 line-range citation remains in the specification.
